messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: eu-west gpu-pool pending queue > 1.2k, pending pods=542, current_nodes=64, max_nodes=64. Autoscaler halted (respecting max). Severity: P1.

mike_oncall: Ack. Seeing elevated 5xx and generation tail latency from hosted-api. Kicking off triage.

sarah_ops: Mike - quick check: is this a cloud hard limit or k8s quota? Javier, any infra constraints we should know?

javier_infra: Confirmed - cloud provider max_nodes for eu-west gpu pool is 64 (per recent safety policy). Cluster-autoscaler healthy but can't exceed that. Many pods pending due to gpu resource shortage.

emily_cs: CS: 3 enterprise customers hitting failed requests, one on a live demo. They're getting 502s. Customers alerted.

mike_oncall: We need a temporary capacity lift + short-term throttling. Plan: request manual node cap increase to 80, apply route rate-limits to reduce new work, and reroute batch-heavy tenants to Dedicated. Javier please start cap request and flag cloud-ops.

javier_infra: Initiating cap lift request. Using internal runbook. Pinging @cloud-ops-bot and opening a rapid change ticket. Command I ran: 
```
cloudctl quotas update --project=redwood-prod --region=eu-west --quota=gke_node_count --value=80 --reason="incident 2976543210 temporary lift"
```
Ticket ID: CO-93412. ETA on approval ~8-12m.

incident-bot: Runbook note: after capacity increase, mark new nodes with taint gpu:temp=true to prevent non-critical pods from scheduling until we remove taint.

mike_oncall: Implemented short-term route throttling: hosted-api /v1/generate soft-limit 50r/s (was 200r/s) to protect tail. Applied via edge-config change.

sarah_ops: Good. Also please flip routing policy for customers tagged 'batch' to prefer dedicated pools. That should shave ~20% off pending queue.

javier_infra: Cloud-ops responded: approved temporary increase to 80 nodes for 30 minutes. Provisioning now. Logs: 
```
[cloud-ops-bot] provisioning_started cluster=eu-west-gpu nodes_requested=16
[cloud-ops-bot] expected_ready_in=9m
```

mike_oncall: Rebalancing in-progress. Manually evicting low-priority pods from gpu nodes to accelerate scheduling of generation pods. Command: `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` (targeting gpulowprio label).

emily_cs: Sending customer update: "We've identified increased demand causing capacity saturation. We are scaling capacity and throttling non-essential traffic. ETA ~10 minutes." Customers asked for credits; capturing requests in CS ticket.

autoscaler-bot: Info: pending_pod_count dropping from 542 -> 410 as new nodes register. Continuous batching remains high but latency slowly improving.

javier_infra: New nodes reporting Ready. Current_nodes=76. Scheduling catching up. Pod pending now 87.

mike_oncall: Observed error rate trending down. Continuing to monitor. We'll keep throttles in place for another 5m after backpressure eases.

sarah_ops: Good run. Action items: 1) Postmortem owner: Mike. 2) Cloud quota request to be reverted at 30m mark automatically by cloud-ops-bot. 3) Follow-up to consider increasing default max_nodes for eu-west to 96 for peak windows.

cloud-ops-bot: Temporary quota increase will auto-revert at 30 minutes (CO-93412). Manual rollback: `cloudctl quotas update ... --value=64`.

emily_cs: Customers updated, two requested expedited credit review. Filed CS-4832.

mike_oncall: Handoff to next oncall in 30m: @sarah_ops will monitor while I write initial incident notes. Closing thread for active triage; will post postmortem link. :white_check_mark:

sarah_ops: Ack, monitoring. If error rate rises above 0.5% we'll reopen pager.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: capacity lifted to 76 nodes, pending pods reduced to 12 in last check. Status: mitigated -> monitoring.

mike_oncall: Thanks team, great coordination. Postmortem ticket created: PM-1129. Assigning to myself for timeline and root cause (policy vs demand).

emily_cs: Thx, closing customer comms loop.
summary: P1: eu-west GPU pool reached configured node max; manual temporary quota lift to 80 nodes, throttling and routing changes applied; mitigation confirmed and monitoring ongoing. Postmortem owner assigned.
